# 礼物一定隐含回报义务吗

**结论先行**：这个命题作为关于**一切礼物**的普遍断言是站不住的。它准确描述的是一种范围更窄的制度事实——莫斯意义上的"总体呈献"（古式馈赠—回赠体系）：在那里，回报不只是被期待，而是**可以被要求**的。把它外推为"礼物"概念的必然成分，恰恰是批评者认为最成问题的一步。

---

## 一、莫斯本人到底主张什么

先要防止一个常见的过度推广。莫斯《礼物：古式社会中交换的形式与理由》（*Essai sur le don*, 1923–24；英文 *The Gift*）的驱动问题**本身就有范围限定**：

> "在落后或古式类型的社会中，是什么法律与利益的规则，使收到的赠礼必须被归还？在人所赠予的东西里，有什么力量使受赠者归还它？"
> （Mauss 1950: 148，经 Hénaff 引述；此处为我自译）

他的答案就是那著名的**三重义务：给、收、还**（[EBSCO 词条](https://www.ebsco.com/research-starters/literature-and-writing/gift-marcel-mauss)概括了这层），以及用毛利人的 *hau*（所赠之物的"灵")来解释"物何以必定回流"。

但有两处关键限定，常被"礼物必有义务"的通俗读法抹掉：

1. **莫斯自己把古式馈赠定性为混合体。** 他反复说这类馈赠"表面自由无偿，实则受约束且含利害"（"apparemment libre et gratuit, et cependant contraint et intéressé"），是"理论上自愿、实际却必须给且必须还"的礼物；而结论中他更明确写道：这个概念"既非纯粹自由、纯粹无偿的给付，也非纯粹利害的有用物的生产与交换。它是在那里开花的一种**混合体**（hybride）"（Mauss 1950: 366–367，见 [Caillé 引述](https://shs.cairn.info/article/RDM_030_0393?lang=fr&ID_ARTICLE=RDM_030_0393)；我自译）。所以即便莫斯也不主张礼物=纯粹义务。
2. **他的用词暴露了真正的对象。** Hénaff 指出：整篇《礼物》里"互惠（réciprocité）"只出现一次，"交换（échange）"却出现近两百次，副标题干脆就是"交换的形式与理由"（[Hénaff, *Mauss et l'invention de la réciprocité*](https://shs.cairn.info/revue-du-mauss-2010-2-page-71?lang=fr)）。莫斯实际刻画的是古式社会中"赠予—回赠"这一**制度**，而非"礼物"这个概念的普遍本质。

此外，莫斯自陈这部作品"只是提示性的、不完整的"，呼吁到密克罗尼西亚、印度支那、西藏、缅甸、北非等地继续研究（[Racine 1991, 摘要](https://doi.org/10.1177/039219219103915404)）——这本身就说明他不认为自己提出了关于"礼物"的终局普遍命题。

## 二、一个批评性二级来源：Testart（并旁及德里达）

**Alain Testart，《赠予批判》（*Critique du don*, 2007）**，先由 1997、2001 年论文提出，后由 François Athané（2011）接续；其要点可由 Darmangeat 在《L'Homme》上的综述清楚读到（[Darmangeat, *Don, échange et autres transferts*, 2016](https://journals.openedition.org/lhomme/28828?lang=en)）：

- **第一条**：否认"古式世界"由单一的赠予原则统辖。
- **第二条（更致命）**：莫斯**从未把"赠予"与"交换"对立起来定义**。于是他的文本里充斥"échange-don（交换—赠予）""dons contractuels（契约性赠礼）""l'obligation de donner（给予义务）""échanges volontaires-obligatoires（自愿—强制的交换）"这类说法。Testart 判定这些是"与方形圆同一性质的**逻辑怪物**"（"monstruosité[s] logique[s]…cercle-carré"，2001: 742；见 Darmangeat 引述）。

据此，Testart 提出的替代标准是**"可要求性"（exigibilité）**——回付能否被**索取**。按此标准，回报义务不属于"礼物"的概念内核，而是莫斯把赠予与交换混同后的产物：制度上可被要求的，才是交换/债；纯赠予则不可被要求。

德里达从另一角度施压（经 [Hénaff, *The Philosophers' Gift*, 2019](https://doi.org/10.5422/fordham/9780823286478.003.0002)）：若把互惠塞进礼物，礼物就成了它所自称之物的反面；对一个**预设甚至强制回报**的姿态，还该不该用"礼物"一词？——注意，德里达并不否证莫斯的田野材料，他质疑的是**术语**。

也需要给出**反批评**，否则不公正：Caillé 与 MAUSS 阵营主张保留"礼物"一词，理由是莫斯本人在标题里就用"交换"（[Caillé 前引文](https://shs.cairn.info/article/RDM_030_0393?lang=fr&ID_ARTICLE=RDM_030_0393)）；[Adloff 2022, 摘要](https://doi.org/10.1332/policypress/9781529226225.003.0003)则读出一个更"莫斯+Caillé"的版本：礼物含有自由与无条件性的成分，不能化约为自利或义务。**所以这是活争论，不是定论。**

## 三、一个当代反例：匿名非定向活体肾捐赠

**匿名/非定向（nondirected）活体肾捐赠**：一位健康的人把一只肾捐给**素不相识**的陌生人，通常匿名，既无从获得物质回报，往往连受赠者是谁都不知道。这不只是设想——[Fleck & Ward 2022](https://doi.org/10.1017/s0963180121001080) 就是一位非定向肾捐赠者 Arthur Ward 的访谈（我与该文均只读到摘要）。

平行且更经典的例子是**自愿献血**。Titmuss《礼物关系》（1970，2018 重版）称：血的赠予发生在**非人格化**情境中，受者几乎从不为捐赠者所知，"因此不可能有个人的感激或其他情感表达"，而匿名制正是要害（[Titmuss 2018, 第五章摘要](https://doi.org/10.1332/policypress/9781447349570.003.0005)）。

**评估**：若承认这些是"礼物"，它们就**证伪了"礼物必产生回报义务"的强普遍命题**——这里既无物质回报的期待，也无个人化回报的可能。

**但要公平地给出反诘**：互惠可以**换一个层次**回潮——普遍化互惠（"哪天我也可能需要"）、社会承认、捐赠者获得的意义感、或"别人也会这样做"的制度性期待。因此这个反例的力量，取决于你把"回报义务"定义得多窄。

## 四、回答"一定吗"

把问题拆成三层，答案就清楚了：

| 层次 | 回报地位 | 例子 |
|---|---|---|
| 可**要求**的回报 | 义务（制度/礼法支撑） | 莫斯式总体呈献、kula、potlatch（Testart 的 exigibilité） |
| 被**期待**但不可要求 | 强倾向，非必然 | 普遍化互惠、人情往来 |
| **无**回报期待 | 自由礼物 | 匿名肾捐赠、自愿献血 |

- "一定隐含回报义务"过强。更稳的表述是：**赠予在各种社会中强烈倾向于编织回报关系，但回报义务本身是特定制度（馈赠—回赠体系、礼俗或法律）的产物，而非"礼物"概念的必然成分。**
- 分歧的一部分其实是**语词之争**：匿名捐肾算不算"礼物"，还是应归入捐赠/慈善/牺牲？这直接决定它是否真的反驳莫斯。所以，与其问"礼物是否一定隐含义务"，更精确的问法是"在什么制度条件下，赠予才附带可要求的回报"。

**证据限制**（如实交代）：本地哲学书库未收录莫斯《礼物》原典（我以作者与书名检索均无命中），故莫斯原文我依赖上述学术来源的**引述与转译**，未能逐字核到原版排印；法国原句我给出原文并标明拙译。医学—伦理文献我只取得摘要，未读全文，因此只能确认"匿名非定向肾捐赠"这一实践的存在，**不能**据此陈述捐赠者的具体动机。

abstract.text: An alternative theoretical framework is provided by Marcel Mauss, whose [1925] 1990 essay The Gift is the main focus of Chapter 2. Mauss made us understand the seminal role that gifts and reciprocity played in past societies, and still play today. His as well as Alain Caillé’s work makes it clear that gifts comprise an element of freedom and unconditionality. They cannot be reduced to either self-interest or obligation; rather, giving, receiving, and reciprocating are intrinsically linked to forms of mutual recognition.

abstract.text: This chapter discusses Jacques Derrida's Given Time (1992), which presents an aporia of the gift that has made its mark and has occasioned many commentaries and a few refutations. The aporia of the gift according to Derrida can be summed up as follows: Giving is always understood as a relationship between a giver and a receiver, an exchange that generates a debt and in the final analysis remains within the confines of economic reciprocity; in this, the gift becomes the opposite of what it claims to be. To escape this logic, for the gift to be truly a gift, Derrida claims, the giver would have to be unaware that he is giving, and the receiver unaware of the giver's identity. Starting with those requirements, Derrida proposes a critical reading of Marcel Mauss's The Gift (1990), a writing where the obligation to give, receive, and reciprocate established by ethnographic inquiries is understood as the core of the gift relationship. Derrida's purpose is not to reject those data, but to dispute the validity of the term “gift” as designating a gesture that presupposes or even mandates the requirement of reciprocity.

RESEARCH STARTER

The Gift by Marcel Mauss

"The Gift" by Marcel Mauss is a seminal work that explores the nature of gift exchange in various cultures, particularly in archaic societies. Mauss challenges the conventional view of economics as a standalone entity by arguing that economic activities are deeply intertwined with social and cultural practices. His investigation centers on the concept of reciprocity, highlighting that gifts are not merely objects but carry moral and social obligations among individuals and groups. In contrasting modern economic exchanges with those in societies such as the Trobriand Islanders and northwestern American tribes, he illustrates that the act of giving is often laden with expectations of repayment, creating enduring bonds between people.

Mauss identifies three key obligations surrounding gift exchange: the obligation to give, to receive, and to repay. He points out that within these traditions, gifts are often seen as imbued with divine or magical qualities that compel further exchanges. By examining rituals like the potlatch—a competitive gift-giving feast—he demonstrates how social status and relationships are negotiated through the act of giving. Additionally, Mauss draws parallels between ancient gift-giving customs across various cultures, suggesting that the interconnection of personhood and objects in exchange has deep historical roots. His work has had a profound influence on anthropology and sociology, prompting extensive research into the intricate relationships between exchange practices and social structures.

Don, échange et autres transferts

Abstracts

L’article prolonge les travaux d’Alain Testart et de François Athané, reprenant l’idée qu’une société sans État n’est pas pour autant une société sans droit et que le critère de l’exigibilité s’avère universellement valide afin de caractériser les différents transferts de biens. Revenant sur la définition de l’échange obligatoire et sur la classification des transferts illégitimes, il explore ensuite les situations intermédiaires entre les formes pures de transferts, qui avaient motivé la réflexion initiale de Marcel Mauss. Il distingue les cas d’indétermination (privilégiés par l’ Essai sur le don ), des cas de combinaison. Plusieurs exemples historiques et ethnologiques sont examinés, en particulier celui du tee de Nouvelle-Guinée, qui se révèle constituer une articulation originale d’échange et de don.

Gift, Exchange and Other Transfers This article extends the work of Alain Testart and of François Athané. It reexamines the ideas that a stateless society is not necessarily a lawless society, and that the criterion of payability is actually universally valid for characterizing the various transfers of goods. Looking at the definition of compulsory exchange and the classification of illegitimate transfers, it explores the intermediate situations between pure forms of transfer that motivated Marcel Mauss’ initial reflection. The article then distinguishes between cases of indeterminacy (given precedence in Essay on the Gift ) and cases of combination. Several historical and ethnological examples are examined, particularly that of the tee in New Guinea, which is shown to be an original articulation of exchange and gift.

abstract.text: This chapter looks at the nature of the gift of blood. The gift of blood has certain unique attributes which distinguish it from other forms of gift. The gift of blood takes place in impersonal situations, sometimes with physically hurtful consequences to the donor. Moreover, the recipient is in almost all cases not personally known to the donor; there can, therefore, be no personal expressions of gratitude or of other sentiments. If the principle of anonymity were generally abandoned, the consequences could be disastrous for givers and receivers as well as for all blood transfusion services. The chapter then presents a classification of the different types of blood donors: the paid donor; the professional donor; the pain-induced voluntary donor; the responsibility fee donor; the family credit donor; the captive voluntary donor; the fringe benefit voluntary donor; and the voluntary community donor.

abstract.text: The fluctuations in incomes inherent in rural communities can be attenuated by reciprocal insurance. We develop a model of such insurance based on self-interested behaviour and voluntary participation. One individual assists another only if the costs of so doing are outweighed by the benefits from expected future reciprocation. A distinction is made between general reciprocity where the counter obligation is expected but not certain and balanced reciprocity where there is a firm counter obligation. abstract.text: This book's author was a pioneer in the field of social administration (now social policy). In this reissued classic, listed by the New York Times as one of the 10 most important books of the year when it was first published in 1970, the author compares blood donation in the US and UK, contrasting the British system of reliance on voluntary donors to the American one in which the blood supply is in the hands of for-profit enterprises, concluding that a system based on altruism is both safer and more economically efficient. The argument about how altruism binds societies together has proved a powerful tool in the analysis of welfare provision. This analysis is even more topical now in an age of ever-changing health care policy and at a time when health and welfare systems are under sustained attack from many quarters.

citations_this_turn.excerpt: This chapter looks at the nature of the gift of blood. The gift of blood has certain unique attributes which distinguish it from other forms of gift. The gift of blood takes place in impersonal situations, sometimes with physically hurtful consequences to the donor. Moreover, the recipient is in almost all cases not personally known to the donor; there can, therefore, be no personal expressions of gratitude or of other sentiments. If the principle of anonymity were generally abandoned, the consequences could be disastrous for givers and receivers as well as for all blood transfusion service
